db_status.title: Database Health & Resource Triage
diagnostic_steps: Verify database status is ONLINE and check system uptime to rule out recent crash loops.
Evaluate CPU, memory, and disk I/O wait percentages against severity thresholds.
If DB status is ONLINE and CPU is normal (<85%), inspect active connections and blocking locks before investigating query plans.
recommended_actions: If CPU > 85% with high disk I/O wait, inspect long-running SELECT queries for full table scans.
Escalate to Infrastructure On-Call if status is OFFLINE or replication lag exceeds 30 seconds.

connection_exhaustion.title: High Connection Utilization & Pool Exhaustion
diagnostic_steps: Check waiting_for_lock count: if high, connection buildup is a secondary symptom of blocking locks.
If waiting_for_lock is 0 and idle_connections > 70% of total, identify the application holding leaked connections.
recommended_actions: If caused by blocking locks, follow SOP-DBA-003 (Blocking Locks) first.
If caused by leaked idle connections from a single service, terminate idle sessions older than 15 minutes and notify the service owner to verify PgBouncer/connection pool settings.

blocking_locks.title: Resolving Blocking Locks & Long-Running Transactions
diagnostic_steps: Identify the root blocking PID (blocking_pid) and check its state and transaction_duration_seconds.
Verify how many downstream sessions (blocked_pids) are waiting on the lock.
Check whether the blocking session is 'idle in transaction' or executing a DDL/DML statement on a critical table.
safety_guardrails: NEVER terminate system background processes or replication walsender PIDs.
Do not terminate batch jobs automatically without human DBA approval.
Prefer pg_terminate_backend(pid) only when transaction_duration_seconds > 300 and blocked_session_count >= 3.
recommended_actions: Propose terminating the blocking session using terminate_blocking_session(pid) to immediately release downstream locks.
Advise the owning application team to add statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.

slow_queries.title: Slow Query & High CPU Investigation
diagnostic_steps: Inspect slow_queries for queries running longer than 60 seconds.
Check wait_event_type: 'Lock' indicates lock contention (refer to SOP-DBA-003); 'IO' or 'CPU' indicates missing indexes or unoptimized scans.
recommended_actions: For non-critical analytical queries causing >90% CPU, propose cancelling the query via pg_cancel_backend(pid).
Recommend running EXPLAIN ANALYZE and creating concurrent indexes for wildcard or unindexed filters.
